name: neon-dj__walk2-v2
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Single final 2D game boss sprite for Virtual Beat Battle, one frame only, transparent square canvas. Input image is the exact NEON-DJ identity reference: preserve helmet, armor pieces, color placement, shield geometry, body proportions and material, change only pose. Keep same 3/4 side-view camera facing RIGHT. Subject: Neon DJ, a sleek athletic humanoid DJ robot about 5.5 heads tall, cobalt and ivory angular armor over dark navy articulated joints. Black wraparound LED visor displaying simple magenta equalizer bars, no text. Circular headphone ear pods each with one short thin antenna. Compact cyan speaker in chest. Exactly two arms, two legs, two hands. Each forearm carries a clearly recognizable circular vinyl turntable shield with black record concentric grooves, cyan rim, magenta center and a small tonearm; shields stay attached. Mechanical boots, no clothing, no cape, no hair. Strong clean navy outlines, precise flat cel-shaded planes and restrained highlights, matching anime90 style not 3D render, not pixel art. POSE walk2: Opposite walking contact pose to RIGHT: near leg extended backward LEFT toe down, far leg extended forward RIGHT heel down; near turntable arm counter-swings forward RIGHT and far arm backward LEFT. Same camera, proportions and ground contact as walk1. Composition: complete uncut figure and equipment centered, 12–15% transparent padding on all sides, no crop even antennas/shields. Face and torso oriented RIGHT except natural recoil. Keep all effects tight. No words, labels, numbers, UI, scenery, floor, ground shadow, floating detached objects, watermark. Genuine transparent background.
CRITICAL pose difference: Camera-near leg (on the viewer's left hip) reaches BEHIND the body toward bottom LEFT; knee on left and toe behind pelvis. Far leg reaches forward toward bottom RIGHT with heel planted. Near forearm swings FORWARD across torso toward RIGHT, its large vinyl shield at chest/waist height on RIGHT side, far arm swings back LEFT. This must be the opposite of the walk1 image in input2 which has near leg forward. Do not copy input2's limb positions. Keep the helmet facing RIGHT. No mirrored body or visor.
